name: 2020 Panel scale estimate, revenue split and performance floor

attribution.legal_posture: UN Panel reporting; some claims reproduce Member State information and remain outside criminal adjudication.

caveats: Panel calculation of $20.4 million under stated assumptions; audit status remains unverified.
The true worker count was explicitly described as unclear because of obfuscation.

statements: By November 2019, a Member State suspected the Munitions Industry Department had dispatched at least 1,000 IT workers abroad, often through subordinate entities or front companies.
The Panel listed clients especially in Canada, China, Russia, Serbia, Ukraine and the United States as targets of disguised freelance-platform activity.

The reported average was about $5,000 monthly per overseas worker, with about one third ($1,700) channelled to the DPRK, producing a Panel calculation of about $20.4 million annually for 1,000 workers.
Annex-linked rules reportedly removed workers who failed to earn at least $3,000 monthly for an extended period.

sources.support: Supports the scale estimate, client geography, one-third revenue split, annual calculation and $3,000 performance floor
sources.locator: PDF p. 52, para. 121 and footnote 153; annex 29
